title: Apache Helicopter
difficulty_source_label: Overall 3, Quant 3, Creativity 3 (1-3 scale); Quant Level - HEAVY
fit_question: Describe a strength and weakness and how each appears in a team setting. Alternatively, discuss a time you persuaded someone with data.
prompt: A US defense contractor manufactures Apache helicopters and needs a new plant to meet increased demand. It is considering Brazil, France, or the United States. How should it determine the decision parameters, and where should it build?

clarifying_info.answer: Three US plants operate at full capacity. One can add an assembly line for $500M; the other two are constrained by residential areas.
The client is the only Apache producer and will sell only to Brazil, France, or the US; Brazil and France would be new customers.

interviewer_notes: This case compares demand, plant economics, and risk across three sites. Provide demand budgets and Exhibit 1 as requested, then cost data. A strong candidate eliminates France once its lower revenue and higher costs are apparent, but full calculation is acceptable. There is no single required answer between the US and Brazil because Brazil earns only about 3% more profit and carries greater country and execution risk.

suggested_framework.summary: Size location-dependent demand, test plant capability and supply chain, compare five-year profit, and adjust for country and execution risk.

children.label: Defense budgets, purchase commitments, timing, and price
Labor, political stability, suppliers, logistics, and quality
Setup, fixed, variable, import, certification, and five-year profit
Government change, currency, labor, quality, and demand assumptions

stages.interviewer_asks: What parameters should determine the plant location?
stages.expected_answer: Size location-dependent demand and price, assess labor and production capability, supplier and international logistics, political and currency stability, and quality, then compare setup, fixed, variable, import, and certification costs over the same horizon. Finish with risk-adjusted profit and strategic considerations.

stages.interviewer_asks: Using Exhibit 1, how much five-year demand would each plant unlock?
stages.info_to_release: Five-year defense budgets are $100B for the US, $15B for Brazil, and $10B for France. Helicopters sell for $100M each.
stages.expected_answer: A US plant captures 20% of the US budget, or $20B and 200 helicopters. Brazil also captures $20B US demand plus 50% of Brazil's $15B, for $27.5B and 275 helicopters. France captures $20B plus 50% of France's $10B, for $25B and 250 helicopters. Brazil has the highest potential demand.

stages.interviewer_asks: What major plant and production costs should be included?
stages.expected_answer: Include property, legal, construction, and qualified-labor setup; material, freight, and sourcing QA; assembly labor, training, and production QA; storage, delivery, taxes, and US import certification. Separate capital, fixed, variable, and location-specific costs.

stages.interviewer_asks: Compare five-year profit for the three sites.
stages.info_to_release: Setup costs: US $500M, Brazil $2B, France $3B. Fixed cost is $100M annually at every site. Variable cost per helicopter: US $15M, Brazil $20M, France $25M. Every helicopter shipped into the US from abroad requires $15M certification.
stages.expected_answer: US cost is $0.5B setup + $0.5B fixed + 200 x $15M = $4B, yielding $16B profit. Brazil cost is $2B + $0.5B + 275 x $20M + 200 x $15M = $11B, yielding $16.5B. France cost is $3B + $0.5B + 250 x $25M + 200 x $15M = $12.75B, yielding $12.25B. France is dominated; Brazil leads the US by only $0.5B, about 3%.
good_answer_signals: Applies import certification only to 200 US-bound units
Uses five years of fixed cost
Eliminates France and frames the narrow Brazil-US gap

stages.expected_answer: Build in the US despite slightly lower five-year profit: $16B versus Brazil's $16.5B. Existing operating experience, skilled labor, stability, currency protection, and easier quality control can justify the $0.5B tradeoff. Validate government demand commitments, consider locking in a US contract, test whether Brazil buys below $100M, and assess commercial-helicopter opportunities. Brazil remains viable if risks can be contractually mitigated.
good_answer_signals: Makes a clear choice while acknowledging either can be defended

exhibits.title: Defense-budget purchase shares by plant location
exhibits.description: Share of each country's five-year defense budget allocated to Apache helicopters depending on plant location.
exhibits.key_insight: Foreign localization unlocks host-country demand while preserving US demand; Brazil adds more revenue than France.

math.question: What demand and unit volume does each site generate?
What is five-year profit by site?

synthesis: Choose the US on a risk-adjusted basis, while recognizing Brazil's five-year profit is $0.5B higher. The US offers operating familiarity, skilled labor, stability, and easier quality control for roughly a 3% economic sacrifice. Secure demand commitments and revisit Brazil only if currency, political, labor, quality, and purchase risks can be mitigated.
common_pitfalls: Applying host-country purchases to every plant
Charging certification to Brazil- or France-bound units
Forgetting five years of fixed cost

extraction.notes: All demand, cost, and profit calculations were independently recomputed and match the source. Deduplication returned NEW despite a similarly themed finished case titled Attack Helicopter; this record follows the required verdict. Reviewed and accepted by Claude 2026-09-30.
